questions.question: In May 2025, which Indian organisation successfully completed the 'Har Shikhar Tiranga' mission by summiting Mt. Kangchenjunga?

options.text: National Institute of Mountaineering and Adventure Sports

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Institute of Mountaineering and Adventure Sports**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **National Institute of Mountaineering and Adventure Sports (NIMAS)** is an autonomous institute under the **Ministry of Defence**, Government of India.
 
• It is located in **Dirang, Arunachal Pradesh**, known for its stunning natural beauty and proximity to the Himalayan mountain range.
 
• The institute aims to promote **mountaineering, adventure sports, and allied activities** among Indians.
 
• **NIMAS** provides training in various disciplines, including **mountaineering, trekking, rock climbing, skiing, rafting, and paragliding.**
 
• It plays a crucial role in encouraging individuals to participate in **adventure sports** and contributes to the development of a skilled workforce for such activities.
 
• The successful completion of the **'Har Shikhar Tiranga'** mission by summiting Mt. Kangchenjunga in May 2025 highlights the institute's dedication to achieving excellence in mountaineering and adventure sports.
 
• Mt. Kangchenjunga, the **third-highest mountain in the world**, is located on the border between Nepal and Sikkim, India, and requires exceptional skill and preparation to summit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Himalayan Club**__

 __
 
• The **Himalayan Club** was established in **1928** in Kolkata, India, and is one of the oldest mountaineering organizations in India.
 
• It focuses on **promoting exploration, trekking, and climbing** in the Himalayan region.
 
• The club is not directly involved in official missions or government-driven initiatives like 'Har Shikhar Tiranga.'
 
 
 
• **Indian Mountaineering Foundation**__
 __
 
• The **Indian Mountaineering Foundation (IMF)** is an apex body for mountaineering and allied sports in India.
 
• It was established in **1957** and is headquartered in **Delhi.**
 
• The IMF organizes and supports expeditions, but the 'Har Shikhar Tiranga' mission was executed by **NIMAS**, not IMF.
 
 
 
• **Border Roads Organisation**__
 
 
• The **Border Roads Organisation (BRO)** is a government body under the Ministry of Defence responsible for constructing and maintaining roads in border areas.
 
• The BRO is not engaged in mountaineering or adventure sports but plays a vital role in **infrastructure development** in remote areas of India, including the Himalayas.
 
• Its primary focus is on **strategic road and bridge construction** rather than adventure missions.

questions.question: Which strategy DOES NOT promote sustainable development in agriculture?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Excessive use of chemical fertilizers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Excessive use of chemical fertilizers** negatively impacts soil health and leads to the depletion of essential nutrients in the soil.
 
• Overuse of these fertilizers contaminates water sources due to **runoff**, causing water pollution and harm to aquatic ecosystems.
 
• It contributes to the emission of **greenhouse gases**, such as nitrous oxide, exacerbating climate change.
 
• Excessive reliance on synthetic fertilizers can decrease biodiversity in soil, affecting the ecosystem’s natural balance and reducing the population of beneficial microorganisms.
 
• Long-term use of chemical fertilizers may result in soil acidification, which reduces agricultural productivity and damages the environment.
 
• This practice is considered unsustainable as it poses risks to both the environment and human health, undermining the principles of sustainable agriculture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Efficient irrigation systems**__

 __
 
• **Efficient irrigation systems** help conserve water by minimizing wastage and ensuring optimal water delivery to crops.
 
• Examples include **drip irrigation** and **sprinkler systems**, which reduce water consumption and improve agricultural productivity.
 
• Such systems are highly sustainable as they address water scarcity issues and enhance the resilience of farming practices.
 
 
 
• **Use of drought-resistant crops**__
 __
 
• **Drought-resistant crops** are developed to withstand water scarcity and adverse climatic conditions.
 
• These crops minimize the need for excessive irrigation, promoting sustainable farming in arid and semi-arid regions.
 
• Examples include **millet, sorghum**, and certain genetically modified crops engineered to endure drought conditions.
 
 
 
• **Crop rotation and organic farming**__
 
 
• **Crop rotation** involves the systematic planting of different crops in the same area across seasons to maintain soil fertility.
 
• **Organic farming** emphasizes the use of natural fertilizers and pest control methods, avoiding synthetic chemicals.
 
• Both practices promote soil health, biodiversity, and sustainable agricultural production.

questions.question: Where was rural development particularly emphasised in the Seventh Five-Year Plan?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The **Seventh Five-Year Plan (1985-1990)** of India focused on accelerating economic growth and improving the living standards of the people, especially in rural areas.
 
• It laid particular emphasis on **rural development**, aiming to reduce regional disparities and improve rural infrastructure.
 
• **Rural capital formation** involves the creation of assets and infrastructure in rural areas to support agriculture, small-scale industries, and other rural activities.
 
• Through this focus, the plan sought to enhance the **productivity of agriculture**, which was the backbone of the rural economy.
 
• **Employment generation** was a key goal, and rural capital formation was critical for creating job opportunities in non-agricultural sectors as well.
 
• Programs such as the **Integrated Rural Development Program (IRDP)** were introduced during this plan to promote rural development.
 
• Focus was also placed on improving **education, healthcare, and sanitation** in rural areas to support overall development.
 
• The plan recognized the importance of **self-reliance** and aimed to provide rural communities with the tools to sustain themselves economically.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Industrial zones**__

 __
 
• Industrial zones are designated areas for industrial development and are usually found in urban or semi-urban regions.
 
• In the context of the Seventh Five-Year Plan, the focus was more on rural development than on industrial zones.
 
• Industrial zones are crucial for manufacturing and large-scale industries but were not the primary emphasis during this plan.
 
 
 
• **Urban centers**__
 __
 
• Urban centers are areas characterized by higher population density, infrastructure, and economic activities.
 
• The Seventh Five-Year Plan did not emphasize urban centers as much as rural areas, given the need to address rural poverty and underdevelopment.
 
 
 
• **Foreign markets**__
 
 
• Foreign markets refer to international trade and economic relations.
 
• While foreign trade was important for economic growth, the Seventh Five-Year Plan focused more on domestic rural development rather than expanding foreign markets.

questions.question: Which of the following schemes focuses on providing rural connectivity through allweather roads?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY)** is a flagship program of the Government of India, launched in **2000**.
 
• The scheme focuses on providing **all-weather road connectivity** to unconnected villages in rural areas across the country.
 
• The primary objective is to enhance **rural infrastructure**, thereby improving access to markets, healthcare, education, and employment opportunities.
 
• It is implemented by the Ministry of **Rural Development**, Government of India.
 
• The scheme is funded by both the **Central and State Governments**, with a major share contributed by the Centre.
 
• PMGSY has played a key role in reducing **rural-urban disparities**, fostering rural development, and supporting economic growth.
 
• It includes provisions for **maintenance** of roads for five years after construction to ensure sustainability.
 
• The scheme is aligned with the larger vision of achieving **inclusive growth** and reducing poverty in rural India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana–Gramin (PMAY-G)**__

 __
 
• This scheme aims to provide **housing for all by 2022** in rural areas by offering financial assistance to construct pucca houses.
 
• It targets **homeless families** or those living in kutcha houses as identified under the Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC).
 
• The scheme offers a unit assistance of **INR 1.20 lakh in plain areas** and **INR 1.30 lakh in hilly, difficult, and Integrated Action Plan (IAP) areas.**
 
 
 
• **RURBAN Mission**__
 __
 
• The RURBAN Mission, also known as the **Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Rurban Mission**, focuses on developing **rural growth clusters** by providing urban-like facilities in rural areas.
 
• It aims to reduce rural-urban migration by promoting **economic development** and improving **basic services** in these clusters.
 
• The scheme emphasizes **sustainable development** through skill development, infrastructure improvement, and livelihood promotion.
 
 
 
• **Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana (SAGY)**__
 
 
• This scheme encourages **Members of Parliament (MPs)** to adopt villages and transform them into model villages.
 
• The focus is on **holistic development** of villages, including social, economic, and infrastructure aspects.
 
• SAGY emphasizes **community participation** and the use of existing government schemes to achieve its objectives.

questions.question: What is the primary aim of the National Urban Livelihoods Mission (NULM)?

__
 
• The **National Urban Livelihoods Mission (NULM)** aims to **reduce urban poverty** by providing sustainable livelihood opportunities to the urban poor.
 
• Its focus is on **skill development**, enabling individuals to become employable in various sectors or to establish their own income-generating activities.
 
• The mission works to provide **self-employment opportunities** to urban poor households by creating support mechanisms such as **self-help groups (SHGs)** and other capacity-building initiatives.

• Another key aspect is the formation and promotion of **urban poor collectives** to support social and financial inclusion.
 
• The mission is a part of the Government of India's larger goal to achieve **socio-economic upliftment** and **poverty alleviation** in urban areas.
 
• It focuses on integrating marginalized sections like **women, differently-abled individuals**, and other vulnerable groups into mainstream economic activities.
 
• Specific programs under NULM include **employment through skill training and placement (EST&P),** support to urban street vendors, and shelter for urban homeless.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 __

• **Providing subsidised housing to rural workers**__
 
 
• This relates more closely to the **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY)** and not the NULM.

questions.question: Which Article allows the President to appoint a Commission to investigate the condition of socially and educationally backward classes?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Article 340**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 340** of the Indian Constitution empowers the President to appoint a **Commission** to investigate the condition of **socially and educationally backward classes**.
 
• The Commission is tasked with recommending measures for their improvement, including steps to eliminate inequalities faced by such groups.
 
• The President may specify the **terms of reference** for the Commission and decide its composition.
 
• One of the most notable commissions formed under this article was the **Mandal Commission**, constituted in 1979 to identify the backward classes in India.
 
• This article reflects the Indian Constitution’s commitment to ensuring **social justice** and equitable development for all sections of society.
 
• The recommendations made by such commissions often lead to the formulation of policies like **reservation in education and employment**.
 
• It aims to address the issues of **discrimination, inequality, and deprivation** faced by backward classes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 330**__

 __
 
• Article 330 of the Constitution provides for **reservation of seats** in the Lok Sabha for **Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes**.
 
• This article is specifically aimed at ensuring **political representation** for marginalized communities.
 
 
 
• **Article 332**__
 __
 
• Article 332 pertains to the **reservation of seats** for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the **Legislative Assemblies** of states.
 
• It ensures that these communities have adequate representation in state legislatures.
 
 
 
• **Article 342**__
 
 
• Article 342 deals with the identification and specification of **Scheduled Tribes** in India.
 
• The President can notify a tribe as a Scheduled Tribe in consultation with the **Governor of a state**.
 
• It aims to provide **special safeguards** and benefits for tribal communities.

questions.question: What is the term used for the persistence of sound in a large hall due to repeated reflections from walls and other surfaces?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Reverberation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Reverberation** refers to the **persistence of sound** in a space, such as a large hall, caused by the repeated reflections of sound waves from walls, ceilings, and other surfaces.
 
• It occurs when sound waves are reflected back into the room multiple times before eventually fading away.
 
• Reverberation is a key factor in acoustics and directly impacts the **quality of sound** in enclosed spaces like concert halls, auditoriums, and lecture rooms.
 
• Excessive reverberation can make speech and music unclear, whereas controlled reverberation can enhance the **richness and fullness** of sound.
 
• The time it takes for the reverberated sound to decay by 60 dB is called the **reverberation time** (T60), and it is a critical parameter in acoustic engineering.
 
• Materials like carpets, curtains, and acoustic panels are often used to reduce excessive reverberation by absorbing sound.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Diffraction**__

 __
 
• **Diffraction** is the bending of sound or light waves around obstacles or through small openings.
 
• It is more pronounced when the wavelength of the wave is comparable to the size of the obstacle or aperture.
 
• An example of diffraction in sound is when you can hear someone talking around a corner even though you cannot see them.
 
 
 
• **Refraction**__
 __
 
• **Refraction** is the change in direction of a sound wave or light wave when it passes from one medium to another with a different density.
 
• This phenomenon occurs due to the change in the wave's speed in different media.
 
• In acoustics, refraction may cause sound waves to bend when traveling through layers of air with varying temperatures.
 
 
 
• **Interference**__
 
 
• **Interference** is the phenomenon that occurs when two or more sound waves overlap and combine.
 
• It can be constructive (amplifying sound) or destructive (reducing sound), depending on the phase relationship of the waves.
 
• Interference is often observed in musical instruments and sound systems.

questions.question: Bal Gangadhar Tilak gave which popular slogan to arouse nationalist sentiments among the Indians?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Swaraj is my birthright**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The slogan **"Swaraj is my birthright"** was given by **Bal Gangadhar Tilak**, a prominent leader in the **Indian freedom struggle**.
 
• This slogan became a **rallying cry** for Indians during the **freedom movement** against British colonial rule.
 
• Tilak voiced this slogan in the year **1917** to inspire Indians to fight for their **right to self-rule**.
 
• Bal Gangadhar Tilak is also regarded as the **Father of Indian Unrest** due to his role in mobilizing masses against British rule.
 
• He was one of the leaders of the **Lal-Bal-Pal trio**, alongside **Lala Lajpat Rai** and **Bipin Chandra Pal**, who spearheaded the extremist faction of the Indian National Congress.
 
• Tilak's idea of Swaraj was deeply rooted in the concept of **self-governance**, where Indians would have full control over their political, social, and economic affairs.
 
• He also started newspapers such as **Kesari** (in Marathi) and **The Mahratta** (in English) to spread nationalist ideas and promote the demand for Swaraj.
 
• Bal Gangadhar Tilak played a crucial role in fostering the sense of patriotism and unity among Indians, making the slogan a symbol of India's struggle for independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Inquilab Zindabad**__

 __
 
• The slogan **Inquilab Zindabad** translates to **"Long live the revolution."**
 
• It was popularized by **Bhagat Singh** and other revolutionaries in the fight for India's independence from British rule.
 
• This slogan became synonymous with revolutionary activities and the spirit of rebellion against colonial oppression.
 
 
 
• **Vande Mataram**__
 __
 
• **Vande Mataram**, meaning "**I bow to thee, Mother**", is a patriotic song written by **Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay**.
 
• It was a source of inspiration during the **Indian independence movement** and became the **national song** of India.
 
• The song was included in his novel **Anandamath** and served as a unifying hymn for freedom fighters.
 
 
 
• **Quit India**__
 
 
• The **Quit India Movement**, also known as the **August Movement**, was launched by **Mahatma Gandhi** in **1942**.
 
• The slogan **"Quit India"** urged the British to leave India and grant it independence immediately.
 
• The movement was a significant step in India's struggle for independence and was marked by widespread civil disobedience and protests.

questions.question: What is the correct way to rename a file or folder using the right mouse button?

options.text: Right-click on the desktop → Select New → Rename
Double-click on the file → Type new name
Right-click on the file → Select Rename → Type new name → Press Enter
Left-click on the file → Press Delete → Type new name

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Right-click on the file → Select Rename → Type new name → Press Enter**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct way to rename a file or folder using the mouse involves the **right-click menu**.
 
• By **right-clicking** on a file or folder, a context menu is displayed, offering several options such as Open, Copy, Delete, and Rename.
 
• Selecting the **"Rename"** option allows the user to edit the existing name of the file or folder.
 
• After typing the new name, the process is finalized by pressing the **Enter** key on the keyboard.
 
• This method is **user-friendly** and allows precise renaming without accidentally opening the file.
 
• It is a widely used feature across various **operating systems**, such as Windows, macOS, and Linux.
 
• Using this method ensures that the file or folder name is changed efficiently without requiring additional tools or commands.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Right-click on the desktop → Select New → Rename**__

 __
 
• This option is incorrect because creating a new file or folder is a separate function from renaming an existing one.
 
• The **"New"** option in the context menu is used to create new items such as folders, text files, or shortcuts, not to rename existing files.
 
 
 
• **Double-click on the file → Type new name**__
 __
 
• Double-clicking on a file typically opens the file, rather than allowing the user to rename it.
 
• Renaming is not directly possible with a double-click unless specific settings or shortcuts are used.
 
 
 
• **Left-click on the file → Press Delete → Type new name**__
 
 
• This option is incorrect because the **"Delete"** function removes a file or folder rather than renaming it.
 
• Typing a new name after deletion creates confusion, as the original file would no longer exist.

questions.question: Which is the first country to develop genome-based rice variety?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **India** is the **first country in the world** to develop a **genome-based rice variety**.
 
• The breakthrough genome-based rice variety was developed by **scientists at the Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI), Pusa, New Delhi.**
 
• This new rice variety is known as **Mukta Vartani**, developed using advanced **genome editing technology called CRISPR-Cas9.**
 
• Genome-based rice varieties are designed to have **high yield, disease resistance, and better adaptability** to climate change.
 
• The focus is to ensure **food security** for the growing population by developing varieties that are more **resilient to stresses such as drought and flood.**
 
• The development of such varieties places India at the forefront of **agricultural biotechnology** and enhances its capability in contributing to global food security.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **China**__

 __
 
• **China** is the world’s **largest producer and consumer of rice**.
 
• It has made significant advancements in rice production, including the development of **hybrid rice varieties**, which are known for their high yields.
 
• However, it has not yet developed a genome-based rice variety like India has.

questions.question: If the 6-digit number N00M49 is divisible by 11, then which of the options below can give a possible correct relation between M and N?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By 11 divisibility rule, difference of alternating digit sums must be 0 or 11k.

Sum of odd positioned digits: N + 0 + 4 = N + 4

Sum of even positioned digits: 0 + M + 9 = M + 9

Difference = (M + 9) − (N + 4) = M − N + 5

Equating the difference to 0: M − N + 5 = 0 ⇒ M − N = -5

**∴ The correct answer is M − N = -5.**

**Given:**

A 6-digit number: N00M49

The number is exactly divisible by 11.

**Formula Used:**

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of the digits at odd places and the sum of the digits at even places is 0 or a multiple of 11.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of the digits at odd places (from right to left) = 9 + M + 0 = M + 9

⇒ Sum of the digits at even places (from right to left) = 4 + 0 + N = N + 4

⇒ Difference = (Sum of odd places) − (Sum of even places)

⇒ Difference = (M + 9) − (N + 4)

⇒ Difference = M − N + 5

⇒ For the number to be divisible by 11, the difference must be equal to 0, 11, -11, etc.

⇒ Case 1: M − N + 5 = 0 ⇒ M − N = -5

⇒ Case 2: M − N + 5 = 11 ⇒ M − N = 6

⇒ Checking the given options, M − N = -5 is a valid relation logically satisfying the condition.

**∴ The correct answer is M − N = -5.**

Divisibility Rule of 3 and 9

A number is divisible by 3 or 9 if the sum of all its digits is divisible by 3 or 9 respectively.

Divisibility Rule of 4 and 8

A number is divisible by 4 if its last two digits form a number divisible by 4. It is divisible by 8 if its last three digits form a number divisible by 8.

Divisibility Rule of 7, 11 and 13 (Combined Rule)

A large number is divisible by 7, 11, or 13 if the alternating difference of blocks of 3 digits from right to left is divisible by 7, 11, or 13 respectively.

__Shortcut Trick__

Multiply the outer numbers directly into the brackets and evaluate terms of the same power.

The x² terms are: 4 × (7/4) − 7 × 1 = 7 − 7 = 0.

The x terms are: 4 × (−27) − 7 × 9 = −108 − 63 = −171x.

The constant terms are: 4 × 19 − 7 × (−14) = 76 + 98 = 174.

Combining them directly yields −171x + 174.

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression = 4((7/4)x² − 27x + 19) − 7(x² + 9x − 14)

⇒ Expand the first bracket by multiplying 4 with each inner term:

⇒ 4 × (7/4)x² − 4 × 27x + 4 × 19

⇒ 7x² − 108x + 76

⇒ Expand the second bracket by multiplying −7 with each inner term:

⇒ −7 × x² − 7 × 9x − 7 × (−14)

⇒ −7x² − 63x + 98

⇒ Now, combine the expanded parts algebraically:

⇒ (7x² − 108x + 76) + (−7x² − 63x + 98)

⇒ Group the like terms together:

⇒ (7 − 7)x² + (−108 − 63)x + (76 + 98)

⇒ 0x² − 171x + 174

⇒ −171x + 174

**__Additional Information__**

Sequence of operations: Brackets, Orders (powers/roots), Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction. Always evaluate brackets before addition or subtraction.

Distributive Property

Formula: a(b + c) = ab + ac. This property is used to expand expressions by multiplying the term outside the parenthesis with every term inside.

Terms in an algebraic expression whose variables and their corresponding exponents are identical. They can be safely combined by adding or subtracting their coefficients.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

CP of 1 dozen (12 pens) = ₹150

SP of 1 dozen (12 pens) = 16 × 12 = ₹192

Profit on 1 dozen = 192 − 150 = ₹42

Profit % = (42 ÷ 150) × 100 = 28%

**∴ The correct answer is 28%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost price of pens = ₹150 per dozen

Selling price of pens = ₹16 each

**Formula Used:**

Profit = SP − CP

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 
 
 

 
 
 
 CP: ₹12.5
 SP: ₹16
 
• 
 

 Profit: + ₹3.5
 Profit % = (3.5 ÷ 12.5) × 100 = 28%

**Calculations:**

⇒ Number of pens in 1 dozen = 12

⇒ CP of 1 pen = 150 ÷ 12 = ₹12.5

⇒ SP of 1 pen = ₹16

⇒ Profit on 1 pen = 16 − 12.5 = ₹3.5

⇒ Profit % = (3.5 ÷ 12.5) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (35 ÷ 125) × 100 = 28%

**∴ The correct answer is 28%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). Selling Price = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

Successive Discount

For two successive discounts of a% and b%, the effective single discount is (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.

Dishonest Dealer

When a dealer sells goods at CP but uses false weight, Profit% = (Error ÷ True Weight − Error) × 100.

questions.question: Which of the following numbers divides 889897?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The given number 889897 is odd, so it cannot be divided by even numbers like 52 and 64.

Check divisibility by 69 (which is 3 × 23): Sum of digits = 8 + 8 + 9 + 8 + 9 + 7 = 49.

Since 49 is not divisible by 3, the number 889897 is not divisible by 69.

By elimination, the correct option must be 59.

**∴ The correct answer is 59.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number = 889897

Options = 69, 52, 59, 64

**Calculations:**

⇒ Step 1: Eliminate even numbers.

⇒ 889897 is an odd number, and odd numbers cannot be exactly divided by even numbers.

⇒ Therefore, 52 and 64 are eliminated.

⇒ Step 2: Check divisibility by 69.

⇒ 69 = 3 × 23. For a number to be divisible by 69, it must be divisible by 3.

⇒ Sum of digits of 889897 = 8 + 8 + 9 + 8 + 9 + 7 = 49.

⇒ 49 is not divisible by 3, hence 889897 is not divisible by 69.

⇒ Step 3: Check divisibility by 59.

⇒ 889897 ÷ 59 = 15083 with a remainder of 0.

**∴ The correct answer is 59.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility by Odd and Even Numbers

An odd number can never be exactly divided by an even number because an even number always contains a prime factor of 2, while an odd number does not.

Divisibility Rule of 3

A number is divisible by 3 if the sum of all its individual digits is a multiple of 3. This trick is extremely useful for quickly eliminating composite options like 69.

Option Elimination Strategy

In objective exams, when dealing with large numbers, checking basic rules (even/odd, sum of digits) helps eliminate 2-3 wrong options instantly without performing lengthy long division.

questions.question: The LCM of the numbers 2.1 and 0.68 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Make decimal places equal (2.10 and 0.68) and ignore decimals to treat them as 210 and 68.

Find the LCM of 210 and 68 using their factors.

210 = 2 × 105 and 68 = 2 × 34

LCM(210, 68) = 2 × 105 × 34 = 7140

Restore the two decimal places to get 71.40.

**∴ The correct answer is 71.4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The numbers are 2.1 and 0.68.

**Formula Used:**

LCM of fractions = (LCM of Numerators) ÷ (HCF of Denominators)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Convert decimals to fractions in their simplest form.

⇒ 2.1 = 21/10

⇒ 0.68 = 68/100 = 17/25

⇒ The numerators are 21 and 17.

⇒ The denominators are 10 and 25.

⇒ LCM of numerators (21, 17) = 21 × 17 = 357 (since they are co-prime)

⇒ HCF of denominators (10, 25) = 5

⇒ LCM of fractions = 357 ÷ 5 = 71.4

**∴ The correct answer is 71.4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF of Fractions

HCF of fractions = (HCF of Numerators) ÷ (LCM of Denominators)

Product of Two Numbers

For any two numbers a and b, the product of a and b is always equal to LCM(a, b) × HCF(a, b).

Co-prime Numbers

If two numbers do not have any common factor other than 1, they are known as co-prime numbers. The LCM of two co-prime numbers is simply their product.
</p

questions.question: Evaluate: (−9) − (−60) ÷ (−6) + (−4) × 8
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Apply the BODMAS rule to solve the expression directly in sequence:

⇒ (−9) − (−60) ÷ (−6) + (−4) × 8

⇒ −9 − (10) − 32

⇒ −19 − 32 = −51

**∴ The correct answer is −51.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression = (−9) − (−60) ÷ (−6) + (−4) × 8

**Method Used:**

BODMAS Rule sequence: Division → Multiplication → Subtraction

**Calculations:**

⇒ Step 1: Perform Division

⇒ (−60) ÷ (−6) = 10

⇒ The expression becomes: (−9) − 10 + (−4) × 8

⇒ Step 2: Perform Multiplication

⇒ (−4) × 8 = −32

⇒ The expression becomes: −9 − 10 − 32

⇒ Step 3: Perform Subtraction sequentially from left to right

⇒ −9 − 10 = −19

⇒ −19 − 32 = −51

**∴ The correct answer is −51.**

**__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

BODMAS determines the correct order to solve math expressions: Brackets, Orders (powers/roots), Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction. Operators of the same level (like addition/subtraction) are evaluated from left to right.

Sign Rules for Multiplication and Division

When dividing or multiplying two numbers with the same signs, the result is always positive [(−) ÷ (−) = +]. When the signs are different, the result is negative [(+) × (−) = −].

Sign Rules for Addition and Subtraction

Subtracting a positive value from a negative value is equivalent to adding their absolute values and placing a negative sign before the result (−A − B = −(A + B)).

 ₹690

 MP / CP = (100 + P%) / (100 − D%)

questions.question: The cost of 18 pens and 4 pencils is ₹200. If the cost of a pen decreases by ₹1 and the cost of a pencil increases by ₹3, then the cost of 19 pens and 3 pencils is ₹151. What is the original cost of 12 pens and 10 pencils?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Original cost of 19 pens and 3 pencils = 151 + 19(×1) − 3(×3) = 161

Let pen cost be x and pencil cost be y. We get 19x + 3y = 161 and 18x + 4y = 200 (or 9x + 2y = 100).

Multiplying 9x + 2y = 100 by 3 gives 27x + 6y = 300.

Multiplying 19x + 3y = 161 by 2 gives 38x + 6y = 322.

Subtracting them yields 11x = 22 ⇒ x = 2. Then y = (100 − 18) ÷ 2 = 41.

Cost of 12 pens and 10 pencils = (12 × 2) + (10 × 41) = 24 + 410 = 434.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹434.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost of 18 pens and 4 pencils = ₹200

Cost of 19 pens and 3 pencils after price change = ₹151

Pen price change = −₹1, Pencil price change = +₹3

**Formula Used:**

Formulate linear equations for the given conditions and solve for variables.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the original price of a pen be x and a pencil be y.

⇒ 18x + 4y = 200 ⇒ 9x + 2y = 100 --- (Equation 1)

⇒ Price of pen after decrease = (x − 1)

⇒ Price of pencil after increase = (y + 3)

⇒ 19(x − 1) + 3(y + 3) = 151

⇒ 19x − 19 + 3y + 9 = 151

⇒ 19x + 3y − 10 = 151

⇒ 19x + 3y = 161 --- (Equation 2)

⇒ Multiply Equation 1 by 3: 27x + 6y = 300

⇒ Multiply Equation 2 by 2: 38x + 6y = 322

⇒ Subtract Equation 1 from Equation 2: (38x + 6y) − (27x + 6y) = 322 − 300

⇒ 11x = 22 ⇒ x = 2

⇒ Substitute x = 2 in Equation 1: 9(2) + 2y = 100

⇒ 18 + 2y = 100 ⇒ 2y = 82 ⇒ y = 41

⇒ The original cost of a pen is ₹2 and a pencil is ₹41.

⇒ Required cost for 12 pens and 10 pencils = 12x + 10y

⇒ Cost = 12 × 2 + 10 × 41

⇒ Cost = 24 + 410 = 434

**∴ The correct answer is ₹434.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Linear Equations in Two Variables

A system of equations a₁x + b₁y = c₁ and a₂x + b₂y = c₂ can be solved using substitution, elimination, or cross-multiplication methods.

Consistency of Linear Equations

If a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂, the system has a unique solution. If a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂, the system has infinitely many solutions.

Convert fraction directly to percentage for easy comparison.

First number ÷ Second number = 75 ÷ 77

**∴ The correct answer is 75 : 77.**

 First Number (A)

 Second Number (B)
 
 77 Parts

 Ratio = 75 : 77

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the first number be A and the second number be B.

⇒ 77% of A = (3 ÷ 4) of B

⇒ (77 ÷ 100) × A = (3 ÷ 4) × B

⇒ A ÷ B = (3 ÷ 4) × (100 ÷ 77)

⇒ A ÷ B = (3 × 25) ÷ 77

⇒ A ÷ B = 75 ÷ 77

Ratio & Proportion

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

To convert a fraction into a percentage, multiply it by 100. For example, 3 ÷ 4 = (3 ÷ 4) × 100% = 75%.

Cross-Multiplication

When two fractions are set equal to each other (a ÷ b = c ÷ d), then their cross products are also equal (a × d = b × c). This allows quick determination of the variable relations.

Applying the BODMAS rule directly, solve the innermost bracket first: (2 − 3) = −1

Next, perform multiplication: 7 × (−1) = −7

Solve the curly bracket: {17 − 7} = 10

Finally, perform division: 290 ÷ 10 = 29

**Given:**

[290 ÷ {17 + 7 × (2 − 3)}]

**Concept Used:**

BODMAS Rule (Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction)

**Calculations:**

According to BODMAS, we must first solve the expression inside the round brackets ( ).

⇒ 290 ÷ {17 + 7 × (−1)}

Next, perform the multiplication inside the curly brackets { }.

⇒ 290 ÷ {17 − 7}

Now, complete the operation inside the curly brackets.

⇒ 290 ÷ 10

Finally, divide the numbers.

⇒ 29

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

BODMAS stands for Brackets, Orders (powers and roots), Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction. This rule is universally used to establish the exact sequence of operations in any arithmetic expression.

Order of Brackets

When simplifying, always evaluate brackets systematically from the innermost to the outermost: Line/Vinculum (bar) → Round brackets ( ) → Curly brackets { } → Square brackets [ ].

questions.question: The value of ((1 + sin A)(tan A - sec A + 1)sec A)/(tan A + sec A - (sec² A - tan² A)) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Put A = 45° in the given expression.

sin 45° = 1/√2, tan 45° = 1, sec 45° = √2

Numerator = (1 + 1/√2)(1 − √2 + 1)(√2) = (√2 + 1)/√2 × (2 − √2) × √2 = (√2 + 1)(2 − √2) = 2√2 − 2 + 2 − √2 = √2

Denominator = 1 + √2 − ((√2)² − 1²) = 1 + √2 − (2 − 1) = √2

Result = √2 ÷ √2 = 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

[(1 + sin A)(tan A − sec A + 1)sec A] / [tan A + sec A − (sec² A − tan² A)]

**Formula Used:**

sec² A − tan² A = 1

sec A = 1 / cos A

tan A = sin A / cos A

**Calculations:**

⇒ First, simplify the denominator:

⇒ Denominator = tan A + sec A − 1

⇒ Now, simplify the numerator. Multiply (1 + sin A) with sec A:

⇒ (1 + sin A)sec A = sec A + sin A × sec A = sec A + (sin A / cos A) = sec A + tan A

⇒ Substitute this back into the numerator:

⇒ Numerator = (sec A + tan A)(tan A − sec A + 1)

⇒ Numerator = (sec A + tan A)(tan A − sec A) + (sec A + tan A)(1)

⇒ Numerator = (tan² A − sec² A) + sec A + tan A

⇒ Since sec² A − tan² A = 1, we get tan² A − sec² A = −1

⇒ Numerator = −1 + sec A + tan A = tan A + sec A − 1

⇒ Now, put the simplified numerator and denominator back into the fraction:

⇒ Expression = (tan A + sec A − 1) / (tan A + sec A − 1)

⇒ Expression = 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Trigonometric Identities

The three primary identities are: sin²A + cos²A = 1, sec²A − tan²A = 1, and cosec²A − cot²A = 1.

Reciprocal Trigonometric Identities

These are: sec A = 1 / cos A, cosec A = 1 / sin A, and cot A = 1 / tan A.

Value Substitution Technique

For simplifying trigonometric expressions without specific angle restrictions, substituting standard angles like 30°, 45°, or 60° often gives the quickest result. Ensure the denominator does not become zero during substitution.
</p

questions.question: Two pipes can fill a cistern, individually, in 70 min and 30 min, respectively. There is a pipe located at the bottom of the cistern to empty it. If all the three pipes are opened simultaneously, then the empty cistern gets filled in 28 min. How long will the pipe at the bottom of the tank take to empty the completely filled cistern if no other pipe is then open?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Capacity = LCM(70, 30, 28) = 420 units.

Efficiency of Pipe 1 = 420 ÷ 70 = +6, Efficiency of Pipe 2 = 420 ÷ 30 = +14.

Net combined efficiency (filling) = 420 ÷ 28 = +15.

Efficiency of Emptying Pipe = 15 − (6 + 14) = −5 units/min.

Time to empty completely = Total Capacity ÷ Emptying rate = 420 ÷ 5 = 84 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 84 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by the first pipe (A) to fill = 70 min

Time taken by the second pipe (B) to fill = 30 min

Time taken when all pipes (A, B, and emptying pipe C) are open = 28 min

**Method Used:**

Total Capacity is taken as the LCM of the given times. Efficiency = Total Capacity ÷ Time.

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Time (min)**
 **Total Capacity**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 First Pipe (A)
 70
 420
 6
 
 

 Second Pipe (B)
 30
 14
 
 

 All Pipes (A + B − C)
 28
 15
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the efficiency of the emptying pipe C be EC units/min.

⇒ Total efficiency when all pipes are open = Efficiency of A + Efficiency of B − EC

⇒ 15 = 6 + 14 − EC

⇒ 15 = 20 − EC

⇒ EC = 5 units/min.

⇒ Time taken by pipe C to empty the completely filled cistern = Total Capacity ÷ Efficiency of C

⇒ Time taken = 420 ÷ 5 = 84 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 84 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Positive and Negative Work

In pipes and cisterns, filling pipes do positive work (+ efficiency) while emptying pipes or leaks do negative work (− efficiency).

Net Filling Rate

When both filling and emptying pipes are open, Net Efficiency = Sum of filling rates − Sum of emptying rates.

Time Taken to Fill/Empty

Total time taken to fill or empty a tank is simply calculated as: Time = Total Capacity (LCM) ÷ Net Efficiency.
</p

In ΔABC, the sum of angles is 180° ⇒ ∠BCA = 180° − (120° + 40°) = 20°.

Since BC || AD, alternate interior angles are equal ⇒ ∠CAD = ∠BCA = 20°.

In ΔACD, given AC = CD ⇒ angles opposite to equal sides are equal.

Therefore, ∠ADC = ∠CAD = 20°.

questions.question: 5 years ago, the age of a father was 14 years more than twice his son's age. After how many years, from now, will he be twice his son's age?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

5 years ago, the gap between the Father's age and twice the Son's age was exactly 14 years.

Every year, the Father's age increases by 1, but twice the Son's age increases by 2.

So, the gap decreases by 1 year for every single year that passes.

To reduce the gap from 14 to 0 (where Father = 2 × Son), it will take exactly 14 years from that past date.

Since 5 years have already passed to reach the present, the remaining time = 14 − 5 = 9 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

5 years ago, Father's age = 2 × Son's age + 14

**Calculations:**

Let the present age of the Son be S and Father be F.

Age 5 years ago:

⇒ Father's age = F − 5

⇒ Son's age = S − 5

According to the given condition:

⇒ F − 5 = 2 × (S − 5) + 14

⇒ F − 5 = 2S − 10 + 14

⇒ F = 2S + 9

Let after 'x' years from present, the Father's age becomes twice the Son's age.

⇒ F + x = 2 × (S + x)

Substituting the value of F = 2S + 9:

⇒ (2S + 9) + x = 2S + 2x

⇒ 2S + 9 + x = 2S + 2x

⇒ 9 + x = 2x

⇒ 2x − x = 9

⇒ x = 9

**∴ The correct answer is 9 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Present Age Assumption

Always assume the present ages as variables (e.g., x and y). Ages 'n' years ago will be (x − n) and ages 'n' years from now will be (x + n) uniformly for all persons involved.

Constant Age Difference

The difference between the ages of two people always remains constant over time. If a person is 'd' years older than another today, they will always remain 'd' years older in the future or past.

Ratio of Ages

When the ratio of ages is given as a:b at any specific time, their exact ages at that time can be taken as 'ax' and 'bx' respectively, where x is a common multiplier.
